You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.

payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Has the image been transformed into a drawing made from chalk?
node.criteria: Use only the saved statuses and image-grounded evidence from n1 and n2. complete: both supports pass, establishing both a chalk medium and a drawing. partial: at least one support passes, but the other fails, so some requested transformation is evidenced without complete fulfillment. absent: both supports fail, establishing neither requested feature. unknown: no support passes and at least one is unknown, leaving progress unresolved. A known failure is negative evidence, not uncertainty; do not infer facts beyond the support evidence. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.
node.binding: Target: the image. Reference: a drawing made from chalk. Combine the independent evidence for chalk medium and drawing form; do not inspect images or add requirements.

node_traces.evidence: Both saved support observations pass: n1 establishes a chalk-like medium, and n2 establishes a drawn rather than photographic form. Together they support the requested chalk drawing transformation.

dependencies.evidence: The edited image has a visibly grainy, smudged surface and soft, chalk-like strokes across the scene, consistent with a chalk drawing treatment.
The edited image visibly renders the giraffes and surroundings with softened, sketch-like drawn contours and shading rather than retaining the source photograph's photographic appearance.

response.content: {"text":"The node’s aggregation rule is too permissive for this case: it treats two passing support checks as proof of complete fulfillment, but the edited image still retains photographic-looking giraffe details and does not clearly establish a fully chalk-made drawing. The reference is partial, so improve the typed decision logic to distinguish evidence of some chalk-like/drawn treatment from evidence that the requested transformation is complete; do not equate “both supports pass” with completion when their criteria only establish suggestive features. Keep the checks grounded in the image and preserve the distinction between a known failure and unknown evidence. The traces are valid and queried, with no transport or dependency failure; the mismatch is semantic/criterion calibration, not missing execution. The high confidence does not resolve that mismatch."}
